newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Chairman of the Australian Cricket Board, Denis Rogers, said yesterday that he would like changes to be made to next year's one day competitions, in order to ensure more fluent scoring in the second fifteen overs. These would include reducing the number of fielders allowed outside the circle. Page 32

The head of the Australian Rugby League competition, Neil Whittaker, has angrily dismissed rumours that the affiliated teams of Manly and Sydney City were planning to defect to the rebel football competition, Super League in 1998. He says it is part of a destabilisation campaign. Page 29.

The Australian Yachting Federation has decided to search world-wide for a high performance manager and head coach to spearhead the effort for medals at the 2000 Olympics. Australian did better than expected in yachting at the Atlanta Olympics, making the finals, and hope to improve on their performance. Page 26

The Australian Rugby Union team will be without its top 60 players in the international competition, the World Cup Sevens, to be held in Hong Kong next month. States such as New South Wales and Queensland have refused to release their players from the current national season to play in the event. Page 28.
THE AGE

Australian runner Kate Anderson has bounced back from her demoralising performance in Atlanta, where she was disabled by foot injuries, to win the 3000 metre race, at a international athletics meet in Hobart. She defeated world-class competitrs such as Ireland's Sonia O'Sullivan and China's Qu Junzia and Zhang Linli. Page 5.

Australian Olympic bronze medallist Rebecca Joyce has had her hopes for the 2000 Olympics revived, after FISA, the world rowing's governing body, decided against lowering the weight limits for lightweight crews. Joyce said she had been preparing to move into the heavyweight class but was relieved that she could stay in her chosen competition. Page 12.

Ericsson Cup defending champions, the Melbourne Knights, maintained their hopes of a semi-final place in the Australian national soccer competition, after snatching a 1-1 draw with competition leader Sydney United. Page 13

The West Australian cricket team is assured of a place in the finals of the national competition, the Sheffield Shield after their defeat of Queensland at the weekend. The team is now heading the competition with 30 points. Page 9.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian golfer Peter Lonard won the Australian Masters on the weekend. He now faces the most important decision of his career, whether to remain with the security of his job as a club professional or to embark on the risky business of being a tour pro. Page 88.

After being warned of a huge damages bill being launched against them, Collingwood Football Club, reversed its previous decision to withdraw form the Ericsson Cup, the Australian national soccer competition, and announced that it would complete the current season. Page 86.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor returned to form yesterday, with a fighting 85 runs against South African provincial champions, Western Province. It was Taylor's highest score in fourteen months. Page 82.

The 99th Austral Wheelrace finished in dramatic fashion on Saturday night. Tasmanian Matthew Atkins overcame disadvantages including finishing third on his heat and a 100 metres gap between him and the race leaders to win the event. Page 79
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Canterbury's James Pickering, considered to be the unluckiest player in Australian rugby league, has been sidelined for several months, following a suspected broken arm suffered during last night's Super League game. This follows a horrific knee injury last year which kept him out of the game for a whole season. Page 35.

Peter Lonard, is the new Australian Master Champion, following his win over Peter O'Malley at the third hole of the sudden-death play-off. The win follows years of struggle for Lonard, whose career has been put on hold following a Ross River fever infecton he suffered in early 1992. Page 33.

The most promising colt to appear in Australian racing in years, Mouawad, is set to race in the Doncaster Handicap as favourite this autumn. This follows his win in the Australian Guineas at Flemington racecourse on Saturday. Page 41

Australian pentathlete Alex Johnson, an overall fifth in the World Cup championships, held at Sydney yesterday, winning the 3 kilometre horse race. It was the best result in his career for the athlete who is now looking forward to the 2000 Olympics. Pag 31.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
